title: Superior level cut forecast error during 120 large Michigan-Huron changes at 1970-2024 issues
abstract: We tested whether added Superior level information helps six-month Michigan-Huron forecasts during large changes. A fixed linear model used current local level and twelve local monthly changes. A second model added Superior level. At 660 issue months in 1970-2024, 120 observed changes exceeded an earlier-data 80th-percentile threshold after seasonal means were removed. Added Superior level cut mean squared error by 6.00% in this group. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was 1.15% to 10.39%. RMSE fell from 0.25080 to 0.24315 m. The gain was not clearly different from the ordinary-change gain. The rarer changes above a 90th-percentile threshold gave an interval that included zero. Future outcomes define the score groups, so they cannot select forecasts in advance. This extends earlier campaign average-skill evidence on overlapping data. It does not identify a physical mechanism or establish operational or flood forecast skill. Revised data, clustered extremes, model choice and conditional intervals limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes and a separate arithmetic audit are included.

display.caption: Added Superior level reduced error in the broad large-change group. Intervals for separate positive and negative departures include zero. Thresholds use earlier data; group labels use observed future changes.

citations.reason: The average forecast gain set this subgroup question. We reuse the source release and primary model design, not code. Data overlap.
